summary: The migration task requests CI-status and active AI dashboard links resolve the current repository identity during the planned mono-to-dotnet organization transfer while preserving permanent Azure pipeline identifiers and historical dashboard data.

reproEvidence.environmentDetails: Planned mono-to-dotnet GitHub organization transfer; no runtime platform or rendering backend is involved.

repoLinks.description: Open implementation PR linked by the issue; it states that it fixes #4985.
Closed portable repository identity foundation referenced as the original dependency.

fixStatus.reason: PR #5002 implements the requested changes and reports focused validation, but it remains open and therefore has not yet resolved the issue on the default branch.

analysis.summary: The default-branch dashboard generator and cached dashboard data still embed mono/SkiaSharp in active GitHub URLs, so those links would be stale after an owner transfer. The linked open PR proposes domain-local identity resolution from explicit input, GitHub Actions context, or a validated origin remote, while keeping permanent Azure pipeline definition 345 and the mono-SkiaSharp display name unchanged.
analysis.rationale: This is a planned tooling improvement rather than broken library behavior: its scope is CI registry, dashboard, tests, and operational documentation. The request and PR describe a bounded implementation with a clear fix path, and source inspection confirms current active dashboard URLs are owner-specific. It is cross-platform tooling work, so no operating-system or rendering-backend labels apply.

keySignals.text: Render current AI/dashboard source links from resolved identities without rewriting historical data.
keySignals.interpretation: The requested change is limited to active links and must preserve historical dashboard content.

keySignals.text: Preserve permanent Azure pipeline IDs/names such as definition 345 and mono-SkiaSharp unless infrastructure deliberately renames them.
keySignals.interpretation: GitHub repository identity and Azure pipeline identity must remain distinct.

keySignals.text: PR #5002 implements repository resolution with explicit input, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, then a validated origin remote.
keySignals.interpretation: A concrete, scoped implementation is available but is not merged.

codeInvestigation.finding: build_cadence preserves a cached prsUrl and defaults it to a mono/SkiaSharp pull-request URL, embedding the current GitHub owner in an active dashboard link.

The committed dashboard snapshot contains mono/SkiaSharp URLs for cadence, workflow source, workflow entry, and footer links; these are the active links the issue asks to resolve dynamically while leaving historical metrics intact.
The package-download tooling defines Azure pipeline ID 345 and documents it as mono-SkiaSharp, confirming that this external pipeline identity is distinct from GitHub repository URLs.

workarounds: Before the portability change merges, maintainers can pass an explicit repository identity to tooling that supports a repository override rather than relying on a transferred repository's old owner-qualified URL.
nextQuestions: Do the pending Automation and Release workflow runs for PR #5002 pass with the final two-commit PR head?
Does the target organization preserve the required Azure and project-board integrations before the transfer cutover?

resolution.hypothesis: Hard-coded active mono/SkiaSharp URLs in the CI-status registry and dashboard will become stale after the organization transfer, whereas Azure pipeline names are intentional stable external identifiers.

proposals.title: Merge and validate the scoped portability implementation
proposals.description: Review PR #5002, ensure its pending authoritative automation and release checks pass, then merge its repository-resolution and regression-test changes. Keep Azure definition 345 and mono-SkiaSharp unchanged unless Azure infrastructure is intentionally renamed.
